title: HTML viewer: rendering a map and navigating map ↔ diagram ↔ guide
description: How renderHtml() turns a map JSON document into a single self-contained HTML file, and how that file's inline script lets a user click through the sidebar tree, jump via guide references, use Prev/Next or arrow keys, and flip to a clickable Mermaid diagram that jumps back into the same node. Key takeaway: there is exactly one navigation primitive, select(id) in html.js, and every other interaction (sidebar clicks, guide [refs], nav buttons, keyboard, and Mermaid node clicks via window.mapSelect) is just a different trigger that calls it.
query: How does the HTML viewer render a map and navigate between nodes, the diagram and the guide?

traces.title: Build time: assembling the self-contained viewer file
traces.description: writeHtml() in store.js calls renderHtml(doc), which precomputes a clickable Mermaid source and a compact markdown dump, inlines all three (doc, mermaid, markdown) as JSON inside a <script> tag, and emits one static HTML file with CSS and JS baked in. When that file is opened, its own inline script immediately parses the embedded JSON back out and flattens every location into a lookup array/map used by all later navigation.

locations.title: writeHtml persists rendered HTML
locations.description: Writes the output of renderHtml(doc) straight to <id>.html next to the JSON map; no templating file, the whole viewer is generated in memory.

locations.title: renderHtml entry point
locations.description: Takes the normalized map doc and returns a full HTML document string with CSS/JS inlined; this is the only function that builds the viewer.

locations.title: Precompute clickable Mermaid source
locations.description: Calls renderMermaid with clickable:true so diagram nodes get `click ... call waymarkSelect(...)` bindings baked into the generated flowchart text (trace 3).

snippet.code:

locations.title: Client parses embedded data
locations.description: On load, the inline client script reads the JSON script tag's text content and parses it back into doc, mmdSrc and markdown — the only data the rest of the page ever touches.

locations.title: Flatten locations for lookup
locations.description: Builds locs[] (ordered array, for Prev/Next and keyboard nav) and byId Map (for O(1) id → location lookup) from every trace's locations; every later navigation action goes through one of these two structures.
locations.lineContent: for (const t of doc.traces) for (const l of t.locations) { const x = { ...l, trace: t }; locs.push(x); byId.set(l.id, x); }

traces.guide:
The whole viewer is one function: [1b] called from [1a] at save time. It front-loads two renderings — a clickable Mermaid flowchart [1c] (feeds trace 3) and a compact markdown dump [1d] (feeds the 'Copy context' button) — then inlines everything as JSON [1e]. There is no server and no build step for the viewer itself: the file is fully self-contained.

When a user opens the HTML file, its bundled script immediately reverses step [1e]: it parses the JSON back out [1f] and flattens all locations into `locs` and `byId` [1g]. Every navigation feature in traces 2 and 3 operates purely on these two in-memory structures — there is no further fetching or re-parsing.

traces.title: Map tab: sidebar tree, selecting a node, and guide links
traces.description: The sidebar is rendered once from the trace tree, then a single delegated click listener handles both expanding/collapsing traces and selecting a node. Selecting a node is the one real navigation primitive: it renders the code snippet, the guide (with [1a]-style references turned into clickable links), and Prev/Next buttons, then syncs the URL hash so the view is bookmarkable. Sidebar clicks, guide links, nav buttons, keyboard arrows and the initial page load all end up calling this same function.

locations.title: treeHtml renders the call tree
locations.description: Recursively turns a trace's tree (refs + label-only group nodes) into nested <ul> markup, each real node showing its id, title, path:line and any anchor-status badge.

locations.title: Sidebar built per trace
locations.description: Builds the whole #sidebar innerHTML in one pass: one collapsible header per trace plus its rendered tree from treeHtml.

locations.title: Sidebar click delegate
locations.description: One listener on #sidebar: clicking a .node selects it, clicking a trace header toggles that trace's collapsed state — no per-node listeners.

locations.title: select(id): the navigation primitive
locations.description: Looks up the location by id, bails if unknown, and becomes the single source of truth for 'what is currently shown' (the `current` variable); every other interaction in the viewer ultimately calls this.

locations.title: Render highlighted code snippet
locations.description: Builds the <pre class="code"> block from the location's stored snippet (or just the single lineContent if no snippet), tokenizing each line with the tiny regex-based highlighter hl().

locations.title: Assemble #detail panel
locations.description: Concatenates breadcrumb, title, description, editor/remote links, the code block, cross-trace links, Prev/Next buttons, and the trace's guide (rendered via the mini markdown renderer md()) into #detail's innerHTML.

locations.title: Guide refs become clickable
locations.description: inline()'s regex rewrites [1a]-style references inside descriptions/guides into <a class="ref" data-ref="1a"> anchors, but only if that id exists in byId — this is how the markdown guide becomes navigable.
locations.lineContent: .replace(/\\[(\\d+[a-z]{1,2})\\]/g, (m, id) => byId.has(id) ? '' + id + '' : m);

locations.title: Hash reflects current selection
locations.description: After rendering, select() replaces the URL hash with the node id (unless suppressed), making every view directly linkable/bookmarkable without adding browser history entries.

locations.title: Detail click delegate
locations.description: One listener on #detail handles both guide/cross-link ref anchors (data-ref) and the Prev/Next buttons (data-go), both resolving to a select() call.

locations.title: Keyboard navigation
locations.description: Document-level keydown handler: ArrowDown/j and ArrowUp/k step through locs[] sequentially (skipped while typing in an input), another path into select().

locations.title: Initial selection on load
locations.description: On first paint, the URL hash (if it names a known location) picks the initially selected node, otherwise the first location in locs[] is shown.

traces.guide:
The sidebar is static markup generated once [2b] from each trace's tree [2a]; a single delegated click handler [2c] does the interactive part, calling [2d] `select(id)` for a node or just toggling a trace's `.closed` class for a header. `select()` is where everything converges: it renders the snippet [2e], assembles the whole detail panel [2f] — including the guide text, whose `[1a]`-style references are rewritten into clickable links by [2g] — and finally updates the URL hash [2j] so the state is shareable.

Three other triggers all just call [2d] with a different id: clicking a guide/cross-link ref or a Prev/Next button inside #detail [2h], pressing arrow keys or j/k anywhere [2i], and the very first render on page load, which seeds itself from `location.hash` [2k]. None of them know about rendering — they only ever compute an id and hand it to `select`.

traces.title: Diagram tab: clickable Mermaid flowchart
traces.description: renderMermaid(doc) turns the same trace/location/link data into Mermaid flowchart syntax: one subgraph per trace, one node per location, edges from the trace's tree, and dashed edges for cross-trace links. When built with clickable:true (as it is for the HTML viewer, see [1c]), every node also gets a `click ... call mapSelect(...)` binding. The diagram is only drawn lazily, the first time the Diagram tab is opened, and clicking a node bridges back into the Map tab's select() flow from trace 2.

locations.title: renderMermaid entry
locations.description: Builds the flowchart text top to bottom: a 'flowchart TD' header, then one subgraph block per trace, then cross-trace links, then optional click bindings.

locations.title: One subgraph per trace
locations.description: Each trace becomes its own Mermaid subgraph titled '<id>. <title>', keeping traces visually grouped and laid out top-to-bottom internally.

locations.title: Node per location
locations.description: Every location in the trace becomes a Mermaid node labeled with its id, title and 'file:line', mirroring exactly what the sidebar/detail panel show for that same node.

locations.title: Tree walk emits edges
locations.description: walk() recurses over the same trace.tree structure used by the sidebar's treeHtml() [2a], emitting parent --> child edges and creating anonymous nodes for label-only group entries.

locations.title: Cross-trace links as dashed edges
locations.description: doc.links (relations between locations in different traces) are drawn as dashed arrows between the corresponding nodes, same data the detail panel's 'links' list [2f] renders as text.

locations.title: Click bindings for navigation
locations.description: When clickable is true, every node gets a Mermaid `click <node> call waymarkSelect("<id>")` directive — the only reason the HTML viewer passes clickable:true at build time [1c].
locations.lineContent: for (const id of byId.keys()) out.push(`  click ${nodeId(id)} call waymarkSelect("${id}")`);

locations.title: Switching to the Diagram tab
locations.description: showTab('diagram') toggles which <main> is visible and, only the first time, triggers the actual Mermaid render — the diagram is never drawn until the user asks for it.

locations.title: Lazy diagram render
locations.description: drawDiagram() dynamically imports Mermaid from a CDN, initializes it with light/dark theme matching the OS preference, and renders mmdSrc into an SVG inserted into #diagram; falls back to showing raw Mermaid source if offline.

locations.title: waymarkSelect bridges diagram → map
locations.description: The global function invoked by a clicked SVG node (via Mermaid's bindFunctions): it switches back to the Map tab and calls the same select(id) used everywhere else, so a diagram click lands exactly where a sidebar click would.

traces.guide:
renderMermaid() [3a] walks the exact same doc the sidebar uses: a subgraph per trace [3b] containing one node per location [3c], edges from the trace tree [3d] (the same tree [2a] renders as nested `<ul>`s), and dashed cross-links [3e]. The HTML viewer always builds this with `clickable:true` [3f], so every node carries a `mapSelect(id)` binding.

On the client, the diagram pane stays empty until the user clicks the Diagram tab [3g], which lazily imports Mermaid from a CDN and renders the SVG [3h] — the only part of this self-contained viewer that needs network access. Clicking a node in that SVG calls `window.mapSelect` [3i], which flips back to the Map tab and calls `select(id)` [2d], landing on the identical detail view a sidebar click would produce.
